sections.title: ENVIRONMENT
sections.html:
Read at daemon startup; all are optional. The first selects which daemon this is. The rest are tuning knobs whose defaults suit a general-purpose deployment and only need changing for an unusual workload. Each knob can be set in the settings table of the daemon's configuration file instead, by its name in lower case without SOCKETLEY_ (see Daemon Configuration), and socketley settings lists every one with its value and where that came from. A number outside a knob's range, or that is not a whole number, is said once in the log and the default is used.

SOCKETLEY_SOCKET#

Which daemon you are, or which one you are talking to. Overrides the default lookup (/run/socketley/socketley.sock when installed and privileged, otherwise /tmp/socketley.sock).

Details

No workload calls for setting it. A deployed node — a container or a host — has a filesystem namespace to itself, so one daemon on the default path is the whole arrangement, and that is what the systemd unit ships. Clustering does not use this variable either: members publish themselves into a shared directory and reach each other over network addresses, never over socket paths. See CLUSTER MODE.

What it is for is running several daemons inside one namespace, which is the development and test situation and nothing else. Two checkouts on one workstation, or two test runs at once, are otherwise the same daemon: whichever process binds the default path first owns it, and every later one silently talks to that process instead of starting its own. Anything that starts a daemon on the default path is claiming the identity the real daemon runs under, so the test suite gives every test a socket of its own.

It selects the state directory as well as the socket, and it has to. Several daemons in one namespace reading one state directory are not several daemons: each restores everything in it at startup, including the others' runtimes, onto ports the others are already serving, and each remove deletes a state file a daemon that is still running it depends on. See WHERE STATE LIVES.

SOCKETLEY_CPUS=max|0-3|0,1,2,3#

The set of CPUs the daemon's I/O thread may run on. Default max, which applies no pinning at all rather than a mask of the CPUs that happen to be online now.

Details

A CPU this machine does not have, or a set that comes out empty, is refused and the daemon runs unpinned with a warning; it is never rounded up to max.

socketley daemon --cpus set says the same thing on the command line and wins when both are given. There the same impossible set is refused outright and the daemon does not start, because a flag typed for this one run is a requirement rather than an inherited default.

SOCKETLEY_CACHE_BUF_SIZE#

Size in bytes of each buffer in a cache runtime's io_uring provided-buffer ring. Default 65536. Larger buffers let one read completion carry more commands, and what the ring costs is its footprint, count times size, against the core's cache — see the section on the receive ring for what was measured.

SOCKETLEY_CACHE_BUF_COUNT#

Number of buffers in that ring. Default 64. Together with the size this bounds how much concurrent traffic the runtime can absorb before the pool runs dry and reads fall back to a slower per-read path; the pool costs count times size of memory per cache runtime.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_KILL_AFTER_RENAME#

A test hook: a sharded storage runtime's commit of a key that begins with this string kills the worker with SIGKILL after renaming the body into place and before the journal record, so a test can put a crash at the one step that leaves a file the journal does not name. Unset by default.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_KILL_AFTER_EVENT#

A test hook: a change of a key that begins with this string, in a bucket that sends events for it, kills the worker with SIGKILL once the change's event record is durable and before the change itself is made, so a test can show that the restarted worker sends no event for it. Unset by default.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_HOLD_CONFIRM#

A test hook: a change of a key that begins with this string is made and answered but the record saying it was made is never written and its events never go out, as a crash right after the answer would leave them, so a test can kill the worker and show that the restarted one sends them. Unset by default.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_PART_LIST_MAX#

A test hook: the bytes a multipart object's part sizes, the numbers of an encrypted one's parts, and its parts' checksums may each take in its header before the list is kept after its body instead. Default 4096, which takes some five hundred parts of unequal sizes to pass; a small value lets a test reach the list after the body with a few parts.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_DOC_FAULT#

A test hook: a directory in which a file named shard.phase (prepare, commit or abort) makes that shard of a sharded storage runtime answer the message of that phase of a bucket document change as a sibling that could not be reached would, without acting on it, for as long as the file exists, so a test can lose a message at each step of the change. Unset by default.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_PROXY_HTTP3#

0 opens no UDP socket beside a --tls entrance, which then offers HTTP/3 to nobody and names none in Alt-Svc; HTTP/2 over TCP is unaffected.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_PROXY_HTTP2#

0 turns HTTP/2 off at an entrance, which then speaks HTTP/1.1 to every client over --tls; see the entrance under the dns runtime's --proxy.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_HTTP2#

0 turns HTTP/2 off, so a storage runtime speaks HTTP/1.1 to every client; see HTTP/2 under the storage runtime.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_HTTP3#

0 opens no UDP socket beside a --tls storage runtime, which then offers HTTP/3 to nobody; see HTTP/3 under the storage runtime.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_HTTP3_ADVERTISE#

The port the Alt-Svc header names for HTTP/3, when a proxy in front forwards UDP from another than the runtime's own; 0 advertises none. Default: the runtime's port.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_HTTP3_CC#

The congestion controller HTTP/3 sends with: bbr, cubic or reno. Default bbr.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_HTTP3_RETRY_AFTER#

The QUIC handshakes under way past which a new client is sent a Retry and must prove its address first; 0 asks it of every client. Default 64.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_SPLICE_MIN#

The size in bytes from which a storage GET is sent by splice from the file to the socket instead of being read into memory and written. Default 65536; 0 splices every body. Below the default a read and a write cost less than the pipe a splice needs, so this changes what zero_copy_bytes counts and how much CPU a GET takes, never what it returns.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_HOT_BYTES#

How many bytes of small objects (up to 60000 bytes each) a storage shard keeps in memory to answer repeated GETs without opening their files, of any key, whichever shard owns it. Default 33554432 (32 MiB); 0 keeps nothing. This changes CPU use and GET throughput and the memory a worker holds, never what a GET returns.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_COMPACT_FLOOR#

A test aid: the fewest records a bucket's journal holds before a storage shard rewrites it without its superseded records. Default 4096. A test lowers it to see compactions without thousands of writes. This changes how often a journal is rewritten, never what it holds.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_HASH_THREADS#

How many helper threads a storage worker takes the digests of large uploads on (the ETag's MD5, any x-amz-checksum- the request asked for or the default CRC64NVME, and the SHA-256 that verifies a signed body: a hex payload hash or aws-chunked signatures), so that the worker's loop is not the one core every upload's hashing has to fit in. Default 3, or the machine's cores divided by the runtime's shards when that is fewer, at least one, so that the shards' threads together do not outnumber the cores; 0 hashes on the loop. The threads are started by the first upload of 256 KiB or more (or of unknown length) and end with the runtime; smaller bodies are hashed in line, since the hop costs more than their digest, and a body that arrives a few segments at a time is handed over 64 KiB at a time for the same reason. This changes CPU use and the throughput of large puts, never what is stored.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_LIFECYCLE_DAY_SECS#

A test aid: the number of seconds a bucket lifecycle rule counts as one day, 1 to 86400, read by the lifecycle sweep alone, which then also runs as often as every second. Unset, a day is a day. It changes when objects expire, so it is never for a runtime holding data anyone wants (see Bucket lifecycle).

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_SHARE_NOTIFY_ALLOW#

The URL prefixes a share link's webhook may begin with, comma-separated; unset, the webhooks of Discord, Slack and ntfy.sh (see Drive, links, media and the web interface).

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_SHARE_BURN_GRACE_SECS#

A test aid: how many seconds the files of a share link that burns outlive its last allowed download, 600 when unset (see Drive, links, media and the web interface).

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_RESOLV_CONF#

A test aid: the file the resolver on a runtime's loop reads its nameservers, search list and options from, in resolv.conf(5)'s form, so a test can point it at a nameserver of its own; /etc/resolv.conf when unset (see What can stop the event loop). A mail runtime's SPF, DKIM and DMARC lookups ask its nameservers too.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_MX_PORT#

A test aid: the port a mail runtime hands mail to a domain's exchangers on, 25 when unset, so a test's own server can be one.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_TLS_CA#

A test aid: the CA file a mail runtime checks an exchanger's certificate against where DANE or MTA-STS asks it to, the system's roots when unset, so a test's own exchanger can be trusted.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_STS_CA#

A test aid: the CA file a mail runtime checks the server of an MTA-STS policy against, the system's roots when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_STS_CONNECT#

A test aid: the host:port every MTA-STS policy is fetched from, the name in its URL still the one checked, so a test can serve the policies of domains it does not own; each policy's own host when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_DELAY_NOTICE_MS#

A test aid: the milliseconds a mail runtime tries a message before a sender who asked (NOTIFY=DELAY) is told it is late, four hours when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_SPOOL_MOVE_MS#

A test aid: the milliseconds a sealed spool segment waits before the few messages still in it are moved and it is used again, a minute when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_DEAD_DOMAIN_MS#

A test aid: the milliseconds a mail runtime holds a domain it found not to exist, or to take no mail, before it looks it up again, ten minutes when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_PUSH_CONNECT#

A test aid: the host:port every JMAP push is posted to, the name in its URL still the one its certificate is checked for, so a test can receive the pushes of a URL it does not own; the URL's own host when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_PUSH_CA#

A test aid: a file of CA certificates a JMAP push URL's certificate is checked against; the system's when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_IDLE_MS#

A test aid: the milliseconds any connection to a mail runtime may be quiet, or its TLS handshake take, before it is told so and closed; unset, five minutes for SMTP, POP3 and ManageSieve, thirty for IMAP, and thirty seconds for a handshake.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_BAYES_FOLD_MS#

A test aid: the milliseconds what a mail runtime's spam filter learned stays in its journal before the first shard folds it into the filter's file; unset, ten minutes.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_IDP_CLIENT_CA#

A test aid: a file of CA certificates the certificate of a client metadata document an idp fetches is checked against; the system's when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_IDP_CLIENT_CONNECT#

A test aid: the host:port every client metadata document is fetched from, the address's own name still the one sent and checked; the address's host when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_IDP_COMPACT_AFTER#

A test aid: how many account changes an idp runtime journals before it folds them into its snapshot, so a test sees the snapshot written while changes go on; 1000 when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_SPOOL_FROZEN_US#

A test aid: the microsecond every message a mail runtime names is named after, in place of the clock, so writers in two shards meet in one name as they would in the same microsecond; the clock when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_QUEUE_SCALE#

A test aid: how many times faster a mail runtime's retries and --queue-lifetime run, so a test sees a message tried again and given up within seconds; 1 when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_BUSY_HOLD_MS#

A test aid: the milliseconds a mail runtime opens no new connection to a domain after one of its exchangers answered 421, doubled by each 421 until a message is taken, to fifteen minutes; thirty seconds when unset.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MAIL_SPOOL_KEEP_BYTES#

A test aid: the bytes of message bodies a mail spool keeps in memory beside its segments, 64 MiB when unset, so a test can have them read back from disk.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_NOTIFY_HOSTS#

A test aid: a file of name address lines that the resolver of a storage runtime's notification webhooks reads before the system resolver, on every resolve, so a test can point a webhook's host name at another address. Unset, a name is asked of the resolver on the loop and then of the system's (see Event notifications).

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_NOTIFY_QUEUE#

The most events a storage shard holds undelivered, beyond which a new one is dropped and counted in notify_dropped. Default: 10000. A test lowers it to reach the bound.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_CLUSTER_QUEUE#

The most changes a storage shard queues for another node of its cluster before it lets them go and sends that node everything instead once it answers (see Cluster). Default: 100000. A test lowers it to reach the bound with a few writes.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_REPLICATION_HOSTS#

A test aid: a file of name address lines that the resolver of a storage runtime's replication targets reads before the system resolver, on every resolve, so a test can name a target by a host. Unset, a name is asked of the resolver on the loop and then of the system's (see Replication).

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_STOP_HOLD_MS#

A test aid: milliseconds, 0 to 3000, that a storage shard's stop waits after its in-flight work has finished and before it lets go of its directory, multiplied by the shard's number plus one, so a test can start a runtime beside shards that are still stopping. Unset, a stop waits for nothing but its own work. It slows every stop and restart, so it is never for a runtime in use.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_START_SPIN_MS#

A test aid: milliseconds, 0 to 30000, that a storage shard's start works through before it opens its store, using CPU as one reading a large store's files does.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_START_SLEEP_MS#

A test aid: milliseconds, 0 to 60000, that a storage shard's start waits doing nothing before it opens its store, as a wedged start would.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_LOG_FLUSH_MS#

A test aid: milliseconds, 100 to 3600000, that a storage shard holds a server access log's lines before it delivers them, instead of a minute.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_RECOVERY_THREADS#

How many threads a storage worker reads its object headers on at a start after a stop that was not clean, 1 to 64. Default: the CPUs the worker may run on, at most 16. The threads end before the listener opens. This changes how long such a start takes, never what it finds.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_RECOVERY_DEPTH#

How many opens and header reads each of those threads keeps in flight on an io_uring of its own, 0 to 256; both this and the thread count are lowered to fit half of what RLIMIT_NOFILE leaves. Default 32; 0 reads one file at a time without a ring. This changes how long a start from a cold cache takes, never what it finds.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_STORAGE_RECV_BUFS#

How many 16 KiB buffers the receive ring of a storage worker holds, a power of two. Default 64; 0 takes the ring away, and every connection reads into a buffer of its own. A connection is lent a buffer only for the length of one completion, so an idle keep-alive connection holds none, and a receive that finds the ring empty is taken by a buffer of its own for that one read, counted as recv_fallbacks in stats. This changes the memory a worker holds and never what it returns.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_TLS_FAILURE_REPORT_SECS#

How often a runtime serving TLS reports the inbound handshakes that failed since its last report, in one line: every 60 seconds by default, 1 to 3600. A handshake that fails is a port scanner far more often than a client, so each one is counted rather than logged.

SOCKETLEY_ACME_DIRECTORY#

The directory URL of the ACME CA that --acme and acme issue use. Default: Let's Encrypt, https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory; its staging CA is https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory. Each CA has an account of its own.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_ACME_CHALLENGE#

The challenge acme issue and --acme prove a name with when none is asked for: http-01, the default, tls-alpn-01 or dns-01. A wildcard is proven over DNS-01 whatever this says.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_ACME_DNS_WAIT#

Seconds between putting a DNS-01 answer where the dns runtimes serve it and telling the CA to look: the time a secondary of the zone has to take the new serial, and the time the delegation probe gives it too. Default 10, at most 3600. A secondary that is told by NOTIFY and transfers on it takes seconds; give one that waits for its refresh the minutes it takes.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_ACME_DNS_PROBE#

The resolver acme issue asks, as host[:port], whether a zone of --dns-zones is delegated to this daemon's dns runtimes, before it proves anything there over DNS-01; it then asks each name server of the zone, by its IPv4 addresses, the way a CA would. off asks nothing and takes every zone as delegated. Default: the first nameserver of /etc/resolv.conf.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_ACME_CA#

A PEM file of the roots the ACME CA's own HTTPS is checked against, for a CA whose certificate no system store holds, as Pebble's. Default: the system's roots.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_GIT_ACCESS_KEY#

The access key git-sync writes into a library with; a storage runtime that starts it gives it temporary credentials of the user the repository is kept for.

SOCKETLEY_GIT_SECRET#

That key's secret.

SOCKETLEY_GIT_SESSION_TOKEN#

The session token of temporary credentials, sent as x-amz-security-token.

SOCKETLEY_GIT_TOKEN#

A GitHub token git-sync reads a private repository with, given to git as an http.extraHeader in its environment, never on a command line.

SOCKETLEY_FFMPEG#

The ffmpeg a storage runtime makes thumbnails and streams with, under /~media/, and the ffprobe beside it, or on PATH, that reads what a film is. Default: the first ffmpeg on PATH; with neither, a media request is answered 501. Read at a runtime's first media request.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MEDIA_HWACCEL#

Where a storage runtime's renditions are encoded: off for x264 on the CPU always, a render node such as /dev/dri/renderD129, or, by default, /dev/dri/renderD128. At its first medium a worker runs one second of test picture through the GPU's whole chain (upload, scale, H.264 encode), with the full encoder and then the low-power one, and uses the GPU for renditions only when one of them works; until it knows, renditions use x264. A rendition keeps the encoder its first job chose, and one whose first GPU job fails before anything is made goes on with x264. HLG is tone-mapped on the CPU, HDR10 on the GPU. vaapi-unchecked:node skips the test run, for a test of that fallback.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_MEDIA_CACHE_MB#

The size in MiB past which a storage runtime removes the media it made, least recently asked for first, from dir/.media/. Default: 10240. The medium made last is kept even when it alone is larger, and none is removed while it is being made.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_CACHE_TTL_SWEEP_MS#

Interval between periodic sweeps for expired cache keys, in milliseconds. Default 500. This never affects correctness: an expired key is not served no matter when the sweep runs, because every read path checks the expiry itself. It controls only how quickly keys that are never accessed again release their memory.

SOCKETLEY_LUA_TIMEOUT_MS#

How long one Lua callback invocation may hold the event-loop thread, in milliseconds. Default 10000; 0 switches the bound off entirely and turns LuaJIT's trace compiler on with it, which is worth about 2.4x on a callback that computes and about 1% on one that does not. See Callback Deadline, which prices both halves of that trade.

Details

This is the default for every script that does not declare its own callback_timeout_ms global; a script that does declare one overrides it. A value that is not a whole number of milliseconds in 0–3600000 is refused with a warning and the default is used.

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_HTTP_REVALIDATE#

Set to 0 to switch off the response cache that plain --http keeps, putting it back on an open, a read and a close per request. Any other value, or the variable being unset, leaves it on. Read when the runtime starts, so a restart picks up a change. What the server serves is the same either way — the cache is revalidated on every request — so this exists for measurement and for ruling the cache out when diagnosing something else.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_KERNEL_TLS#

Set to 0 to keep every TLS record in this process. Otherwise a TLS 1.3 connection of a server, a storage or a proxy that sends a file or object over 256 KiB, a TCP proxy's client a backend streams that much to, or an HTTP/1.1 proxy's client an answer's body of that known length goes to, changes its send key and hands the new one to the kernel's TLS layer, which then encrypts what is sent — by sendfile from the page cache, or spliced from the backend — at about half the CPU of encrypting a copy here. A connection that never asks for that much stays as it was, since for small answers the copy encrypted here costs less. HTTP/2 connections are never moved. Needs the kernel's tls module (modprobe tls); without it the connection goes on in user space under its new key and the runtime says so once in its log. Read when the runtime starts.

Details

Inherited by worker processes, which have no command line of their own.

SOCKETLEY_PROXY_SPLICE#

A --protocol tcp proxy splices a pair from its first byte to its last, instead of only while a side streams. Unset by default; any value other than 0 turns it on. Read once per process and inherited by worker processes.

Details

Without it each side of a pair decides for itself. It copies through a buffer until four reads in a row have filled it — a stream — and then moves its bytes with splice(2) through a pipe, called on the event loop with both sockets non-blocking for the call, never through io_uring, whose splice is an io-wq hand-off per transfer. Four splices in a row that would not have filled the buffer are messages, and the side goes back to copying and gives its pipe back. Each switch waits until nothing of the other path is in flight or queued, so no byte overtakes another. One core, loopback, through the proxy:

                        copy             adaptive         from the first byte
4 GB stream             3.4-4.2 GB/s     9.3-9.9 GB/s     10.1 GB/s
  CPU per GB            0.24-0.30 s      0.08-0.11 s      0.08-0.10 s
64 B messages, 32 conns 6.95 us           6.86 us          10.36 us
4 KB messages           7.41 us           7.37 us          9.28 us

So the variable is for measuring, not for speed. A TLS listener or TLS backend never splices, nor does a pair with a 127.0.0.1 leg while the daemon runs with --fast-lo, a proxy with an on_proxy_request or on_proxy_response hook — the kernel moves those bytes without the script ever seeing them — or one with a --rate-limit or --global-rate-limit, charged per read.

SOCKETLEY_FAST_LO#

Set by a daemon started with --fast-lo once the shortcut is attached, to own, all or trust, so its workers keep a proxied pair with a 127.0.0.1 leg off splice. Not a setting: the daemon clears any inherited value at startup.

SOCKETLEY_NAPI_BUSY_POLL_US#

Enable io_uring NAPI busy polling with this timeout in microseconds. Unset by default. Trades CPU for lower receive latency on busy links.

SOCKETLEY_HUGEPAGE#

Set to 0 to stop cache workers asking glibc for transparent huge pages. On by default and only a cache asks: its hot path walks a keyed structure larger than the TLB covers, which is what a huge page is for, and a server measured no gain for the extra resident memory. The tunable is read by glibc at process startup, so the daemon puts it in the worker's environment at exec — a running process cannot ask for itself.

SOCKETLEY_RECV_MULTISHOT#

Set to 0 to arm one read at a time instead of a multishot receive. On wherever the kernel supports it. A multishot arm is one submission for a stream of messages instead of one per message; the switch exists so the two can be measured against each other on one binary.

SOCKETLEY_RECV_BUNDLE#

Set to 0 to stop packing several provided buffers into one receive (IORING_RECVSEND_BUNDLE). On where the kernel supports it, which is probed once rather than assumed, and it falls back to the plain multishot arm wherever the flag is refused.

Details

Both of these read only the exact string 0. SOCKETLEY_RECV_MULTISHOT=off leaves multishot on, which is the opposite of what it looks like. The SOCKETLEY_NO_* switches below take the other rule: any value except 0 turns the thing off.

SOCKETLEY_NO_SHARD_MESH#

Any value but 0 stops shards linking to each other directly; they relay through the daemon instead. The daemon logs that it is off at startup. It is the measurement control for the mesh, so the two paths differ in the route alone and not in the build.

SOCKETLEY_NO_PEER_LINKS#

Any value but 0 stops runtimes opening direct links to their peers, for the same reason and read the same way.

SOCKETLEY_NO_COMPANION#

Any value but 0 stops a unix-socket listener being placed beside a port.

RES_OPTIONS#

Not read by socketley — passed to glibc's resolver, and set for worker processes when you have not set one yourself. The default is timeout:1 attempts:2.

Details

It is set because getaddrinfo(3) blocks the thread that calls it, and in a worker that thread is the event loop with the daemon's control socket armed on the same ring: while a lookup waits, stop and stats go unanswered. glibc's own default is five seconds twice, which against a nameserver that drops packets measured 10.0 s for one lookup — and a client re-resolves on every reconnect once its cached address stops accepting. One second twice has the same ceiling as two seconds once and still retries a lost packet.

Set it yourself and yours is used unchanged, for the daemon and every worker. Raise it if a slow but working nameserver is being given up on; the cost of giving up is one more reconnect round, not a failed runtime.

EDITOR , VISUAL#

Which editor socketley edit opens when given no flags. VISUAL is tried first.

TMPDIR#

Where that editor's temporary file is written. It holds the runtime's entire configuration while it is open — for a cache that includes master_pw, so point this at a directory of your own if /tmp is shared. The file is created 0600 and removed when the editor exits.

SOCKETLEY_DNS_CACHE_MS#

How long socketley.http() reuses a resolved address before asking the resolver again, in milliseconds. Default 60000. 0 disables reuse and makes every call resolve, which is what it did before.

Details

It is a ceiling and not a promise. A connect to the cached address that is refused, or that times out, drops the entry at once — so an endpoint that moved is followed on the next call, and this only decides how long one that moved without refusing stays wrong, which is the case where something else answers on the old address.

Worth knowing why it exists: getaddrinfo(3) blocks the thread that calls it, glibc caches nothing of its own, and in a worker that thread is the event loop. Every other resolver in this daemon is bounded by something — a client and a server re-resolve at most once per second of reconnect backoff, a proxy once per thirty-second sweep, the rest run once at start. socketley.http() was the exception: it resolved on every call. It now asks on a thread of its own and gives up at the call's deadline, so a resolver that does not answer costs a call its timeout rather than the loop every retry the resolver makes.

SOCKETLEY_RAFT_TICK_MS#

The Raft tick of a daemon started with --raft-listen, in milliseconds. Default 100; the election timeout is ten ticks to twenty, and a heartbeat is sent every tick, so every member of one cluster should use the same value.

SOCKETLEY_RAFT_COMPACT_EVERY#

How many applied Raft entries go by between snapshots. Default 1000. A small value makes a joining node catch up through a snapshot, which is what the test suite sets it for.

SOCKETLEY_CONFIG#

Path to the daemon configuration file.

The set of CPUs the daemon's I/O thread may run on. Default max, which applies no pinning at all rather than a mask of the CPUs that happen to be online now.

Size in bytes of each buffer in a cache runtime's io_uring provided-buffer ring. Default 65536. Larger buffers let one read completion carry more commands, and what the ring costs is its footprint, count times size, against the core's cache — see the section on the receive ring for what was measured.

Number of buffers in that ring. Default 64. Together with the size this bounds how much concurrent traffic the runtime can absorb before the pool runs dry and reads fall back to a slower per-read path; the pool costs count times size of memory per cache runtime.

A test hook: a sharded storage runtime's commit of a key that begins with this string kills the worker with SIGKILL after renaming the body into place and before the journal record, so a test can put a crash at the one step that leaves a file the journal does not name. Unset by default.

Unset by default.

Unset by default.

0 turns HTTP/2 off, so a storage runtime speaks HTTP/1.1 to every client; see HTTP/2 under the storage runtime.
0 opens no UDP socket beside a --tls storage runtime, which then offers HTTP/3 to nobody; see HTTP/3 under the storage runtime.
The port the Alt-Svc header names for HTTP/3, when a proxy in front forwards UDP from another than the runtime's own; 0 advertises none. Default: the runtime's port.
The congestion controller HTTP/3 sends with: bbr, cubic or reno. Default bbr.
The QUIC handshakes under way past which a new client is sent a Retry and must prove its address first; 0 asks it of every client. Default 64.

The size in bytes from which a storage GET is sent by splice from the file to the socket instead of being read into memory and written. Default 65536; 0 splices every body. Below the default a read and a write cost less than the pipe a splice needs, so this changes what zero_copy_bytes counts and how much CPU a GET takes, never what it returns.

How many bytes of small objects (up to 60000 bytes each) a storage shard keeps in memory to answer repeated GETs without opening their files, of any key, whichever shard owns it. Default 33554432 (32 MiB); 0 keeps nothing. This changes CPU use and GET throughput and the memory a worker holds, never what a GET returns.

A test aid: the fewest records a bucket's journal holds before a storage shard rewrites it without its superseded records. Default 4096. A test lowers it to see compactions without thousands of writes. This changes how often a journal is rewritten, never what it holds.

How many helper threads a storage worker takes the digests of large uploads on (the ETag's MD5, any x-amz-checksum- the request asked for or the default CRC64NVME, and the SHA-256 that verifies a signed body: a hex payload hash or aws-chunked signatures), so that the worker's loop is not the one core every upload's hashing has to fit in. A test aid: the number of seconds a bucket lifecycle rule counts as one day, 1 to 86400, read by the lifecycle sweep alone, which then also runs as often as every second. Unset, a day is a day.
